svg.aria-label: The spirit of gold: five readings that run from the metal to practice, and a shadow side where gold points at itself
svg.title: The spirit of gold — five readings and one tension
svg.desc: Five rows, each running from what gold physically does, to what traditions read in it, to what it asks of practice: luminosity, incorruptibility, refinement, placelessness and preciousness. Below, a shadow row: gold wanted for itself points at itself, becomes idol and vanity, and is answered by keeping gold in its place.
svg.text: Each reading starts in something the metal does, and ends in something it asks of practice
divine light: the building lit from within; the Buddha’s
golden skin, his words the “golden mouth” (金口)
Procopius · Pseudo-Dionysius · DN 30 · Kyoto National Museum
let the work receive it, not make it
the deathless: “gold is immortality”; gods with flesh
of gold; an elixir that makes the body incorruptible
Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa · Book of the Heavenly Cow · Ge Hong
the freed mind, “pliant, malleable, luminous”; the soul
tried in fire and coming forth as gold
heaven as no-where: the gold ground, the Pure Land’s
golden earth, a city of “pure gold, like clear glass”
Pächt on the gold ground · Amitābha Sutra · Revelation 21
offering and merit: scripture written in gold; the mind
konshi kindei · Blue Qur’an · Heike Nōkyō · Suger
when the sign is taken for the sacred itself
idol and vanity: the golden calf hailed as god;
“she dresses her stones in gold and lets her sons go naked”
Practice lines are Shinsei readings, not quotations. Sources and discussion: Gold in Spiritual Arts and Scriptures.
